title: water for Karna
hook: at the river, with water in their hands for the dead, Kunti finally tells her sons who Karna was
carry: tarpan: water for every one we lost
tomorrow: why does Krishna let Bhishma do the teaching?

segments.voice: Yesterday in Stri, Gandhari cursed Krishna, and he stayed steady. Your line was sthitaprajna, steady even when the curse comes.

Water is the last thing the living can give the dead. After the fires on the field are lit, the whole household walks down to the Ganga: the Pandavas, Dhritarashtra, Gandhari, Kunti, the widows of both sides. One by one they step into the river and offer water for each person they lost, a father, a brother, a son, a teacher. A quiet, orderly rite after so much noise. And in the middle of it, Kunti tells her sons something she has carried their whole lives.
screen: `THE FIRES ARE LIT.` → `EVERYONE GOES TO THE GANGA.` → `KUNTI SPEAKS.`

segments.voice: Kunti asks her sons to offer water for one more warrior: Karna. The brothers are puzzled. Karna was the enemy, the charioteer's son, the man Arjuna killed. Why him? He was your eldest brother, Kunti tells them. My son, born to me from the sun god before I married your father. I set him adrift as a baby, and I never told you. The Pandavas are stunned. Yudhishthira is crushed. Soon after, as the next book opens, he remembers how Karna's feet resembled Kunti's, and how his anger used to drain away when he looked at them. Now he understands why. He offers the water for Karna himself, and brings Karna's family into the rites. This is a rite Hindus still keep. It's called tarpan: water poured from cupped hands for the ones who have died, often standing in a river, often with sesame seeds, naming each one. Families offer it after a death, and again every year, especially in Pitru Paksha, the fortnight for the ancestors. The teaching underneath: the living owe the dead remembrance, and nobody belongs off the list. Karna was left off until a woman spoke. So Stri ends at the river. The women speak, and the winners learn what their victory cost. Today, think of who's missing from your own list: the relative nobody mentions, the friend you lost touch with.
screen: `"OFFER WATER FOR KARNA"` · `"HE WAS YOUR ELDEST BROTHER"` · `TARPAN: WATER FOR THE DEAD` · then, large: `NOBODY OFF THE LIST`

segments.voice: Cup your hands in your lap as if holding a little water, the way it's held for tarpan. Bring to mind someone you've lost, or someone you're no longer close to. Breathe in and remember one true thing about them; breathe out and tip your hands, as if pouring the water out for them, with anything you never said or never knew. If you pray, you can say their name to God. If you don't, simply say it in your heart.
Stri. Woman. The book that ends at the river, with tarpan for the dead and Kunti's secret about Karna.
Your line: tarpan, water for every one we lost. Tomorrow, Yudhishthira goes to Bhishma on the bed of arrows. Day eight hundred sixty, done.
